title: Hot Air Balloon
strapline: Fire the burner, drop the ballast, and drift up over the rooftops to see the world from the sky.
intent: Children explore a gentle idea of forces — hot air lifts, weight pulls down, drop the sandbags to rise.
Children imagine a bird's-eye view, describing what the world looks like from high above.
Children build and steer a basket big enough to climb into, planning and adapting the design.
Children use rich descriptive and positional language — up, higher, over, below, drifting.
Children ask real questions about flight, air and how things get off the ground.
implementation: Provide a big basket or crate for children to climb into, with a 'burner' to fire and sandbags to drop.
Model the forces talk simply: 'fire the burner to go up, drop a sandbag to go higher, let the air cool to come down'.
Try real lift experiments alongside — a paper bag over warm air, feathers and tissue floating, heavy things dropping.
Prompt the aerial view: 'you're high above the nursery now — what can you see down below?'
Feed in positional language constantly — up, higher, over the trees, below the clouds, coming down.
Add a map of where they might drift to and a logbook for the pilots to fill in.
Follow children's questions about how the balloon flies and what holds it up.
key_questions: How do we make the balloon go up — and how do we come back down?
You're high in the sky now — what can you see down below?
Why do you think hot air makes the balloon rise?
What should we drop to go a bit higher?
Where shall we drift to today, and what will we pass on the way?

impact.text: Children explore lift and weight, firing the burner and dropping ballast to rise and fall.
Children describe the world from above using rich, imaginative language.
Children use positional and comparative words throughout — up, higher, over, below, drifting down.
Children design and adapt a balloon and basket, changing the plan when it doesn't work.
Children ask real questions about flight and air and predict what will happen.
Children invent and sustain an imaginative journey with others.

enhancements: A big basket or crate to climb into, with rope rigging.
A 'burner' (a torch or a red streamer fan) and cloth sandbags to drop.
Lift experiments: warm air, tissue, feathers, and heavy things to compare.
A fabric balloon canopy hung above the basket.
A map of where to drift and a pilot's logbook.
Binoculars for spotting what's far below.
Photos of real hot air balloons rising over a landscape.

playing_exploring: Children imagine floating high above everything they know.
They test how the balloon rises and falls by playing the forces.
active_learning: Children rebuild and re-rig the basket until it feels ready to fly.
They stay with the flight, steering it somewhere and back.
creating_thinking: Children work out how to go up and down and solve the design problems.
They imagine the view and describe a world seen from the sky.
